messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a weird failure mode with streaming + retry in prod last night. Client disconnected, edge retried, and the retried request produced doubled tokens and inconsistent cookies. Anyone seen similar?

riley: yeah i noticed a spike in duplicate outputs around 03:12 UTC. logs show client -> edge: FIN, edge retried to upstream immediately. looks like we didn't check for any upstream partial response before retrying.

sam: do we have a clear contract for what counts as retryable during an active stream? i thought the rule was: if noop response body or no upstream bytes -> safe to retry. but seems we made that decision earlier only for http/1 POST bodies. streaming semantics are fuzzy.

taylor: the tricky bit is distinguishing "client aborted while upstream hasn't emitted any stable token" vs "mid-stream disconnect after some tokens". for the former retry is ok, for the latter we must not retry because app state changed.

alex: exactly. example: LLModel returns partial tokens, saves state server-side. client disconnect -> edge retries -> new replica resumes from start -> model emits overlapping tokens -> duplicates.

riley: proposal: require an explicit handshake/trailer from upstream to mark retry-safe window. e.g. trailers: retry-safe=true once kv-cache flushed. otherwise treat as non-retryable.

sam: +1 but we need a backward-compatible toggle. customers with older models will break. suggest config flag on route: streaming_retry_policy: { mode: conservative|optimistic, max_retries: N }

taylor: also consider a retry-budget per-client-session so hedging doesn't cause duplicate in-flight streams across replicas. we have hedging in the gateway that fires within 50ms; that plus a retry triggers two active generators.

infra-bot: incident INC-2026-47 created: streaming duplicate outputs observed. assigned to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-12T03:30:00Z started to canary on dedicated.

sam: rough config sketch i hacked together:```
edge.runtime.retry_policy:
  type: "streaming-aware"    # conservative | streaming-aware
  max_retries: 1
  require_upstream_safe_trailer: true
  safe_trailer_key: "x-rw-retry-safe"
  hedging_window_ms: 80
```

alex: good start. semantics we need to nail in the RFC: 1) when edge receives client FIN/GOAWAY, only allow retry if no upstream tokens emitted and upstream has not set any session state; 2) if upstream emits any tokens, abort retry path and bubble 499; 3) we expose a trailer key that upstreams MAY set to indicate safe-to-retry; 4) hedging should be aware of retry state and cancel duplicates deterministically.

riley: for 1) we need signal plumbing from runtime -> gateway: token-emitted bool, session-write hints (e.g., kv-cache touches). do we have that instrumentation now?

sam: runtime can emit event headers: x-rw-token-emitted: true after first chunk, x-rw-session-dirty: true if it touched model state. small perf cost but doable.

taylor: downside: forces upstream model servers to opt-in to new headers. fallback behavior: if headers missing, treat as conservative (no retry). that prevents accidental duplication.

alex: agree on conservative default. want RFC to propose opt-in path plus operators can set route to optimistic for internal services. also need metrics: duplicate-responses count, aborted-retries, hedged-active-count.

sam: i'll draft the RFC with concrete state machine and config knobs. will add example nginx/envoy filter snippets to demonstrate trailer inspection and abort semantics.

alex: thanks — @sam can you take ownership of the PR? i'll review and schedule arch sync. aiming for opt-in canary in 2 weeks. :thumbsup:

taylor: one last note — think about websockets/v2 long-poll where clients expect reconnection. we should document clear differences between reconnect and retry.

riley: noted. logging pointer: sample log lines in case of duplicate generation: 
```
[edge] client_disconnect ts=... session_id=... tokens_emitted=true retry_allowed=false action=abort_to_client
[edge] retry_attempt ts=... hedged=false upstream_reply=partial tokens_count=12
```

alex: perfect. sam, ping when PR ready. closing the loop here.
